newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, distant months slip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, distant months slip.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended mixed on Monday, as distant months turned into negative territory on the yen's slight rebound against the dollar late in the day, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from five yen per gram lower to eight yen firmer. Most-active benchmark February was off three yen at 1,382 yen.
Activity was lacklustre as market participants retreated to the sidelines due to holidays in overseas markets.
Spot gold was quoted at $349.75/350.50 per ounce at 0729 GMT, compared with Friday's Tokyo close of $350.00/40.

One focus was the performace of the U.S. stock market after holidays. "The U.S. stock market appears vulnerable to downside risks. We are watching to see whether gold will benefit from any downside corrections in the U.S. stock market," one trading house trader said.
Platinum futures were mostly firmer as a break through the psychological resistance level at 1,460 yen fuelled short-covering ahead of the close. Palladium futures ended mixed in directionless trade.
Platinum futures ranged from one yen per gram lower to 15 yen up. Benchmark February was up nine yen at 1,469 yen.
Benchmark February palladium was up one yen at 570 yen.
Although it was still uncertain when the Japan-Russia talks for platinum group export contracts will be held, the Russian factor is more likely to pressure prices than push them up.

"I think it's a matter of time before Russia resumes its exports of platinum group metals to Japan. Unless the Russian exports are delayed by another two or three months, platinum group metal prices are more likely to go down rather than up," one trading house trader said.
Benchmark February silver was up 0.2 yen per 10 grams at 204.2 yen.
